source.scope: targeted high-risk unheaded prose/example audit for selected pinned-core h3 sections

policy: Selection is risk-based, not exhaustive. REVIEWED means the complete h3 fragment was inspected for engineering semantics hidden below headings; it does not claim paragraph parity for unselected sections.

rows.title: Effect-hooks
rows.selection_reason: React effect timing/dependencies are lifecycle-sensitive and easy to misunderstand from heading-only mapping.
rows.note: Read full effect-hook fragment. Render -> post-render effect -> promise completion -> state-triggered rerender and empty dependency behavior are covered by existing render/async/promise/effect concepts. No additional unheaded concept required.

rows.title: Same origin policy and CORS
rows.selection_reason: Same-origin/CORS is a browser security boundary with important request/response semantics.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: origin = scheme+host+port, browser enforcement, Access-Control-Allow-Origin and restrictive production allowlisting are represented by the existing same-origin/CORS concept and ready card.

rows.title: Error handling
rows.selection_reason: HTTP error mapping often contains multiple failure classes and transport/domain boundary details.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: null/not-found vs malformed identifier vs rejected/internal failure, status mapping and diagnostic logging are covered by error taxonomy, promise propagation and server-debugging concepts.

rows.title: Problems of Token-based authentication
rows.selection_reason: Token expiry, revocation and server-side sessions materially affect authentication authority.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed. Short-lived JWTs versus server-side session state, revocation lookup cost, Redis/opaque-token/cookie alternatives are intentionally covered under the broader token/session revocation authority concept rather than split into a duplicate node.

rows.title: Saving the token to the browser's local storage
rows.selection_reason: Browser credential persistence changes XSS exposure, reload behavior and logout/session semantics.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: origin-scoped persistent string storage, JSON serialize/parse, reload restoration via effect and logout removal are covered by browser credential persistence plus effect lifecycle. BodySense card compares this course localStorage approach with in-memory access token + refresh authority.

rows.title: Searching for content in a component
rows.selection_reason: Testing Library query semantics encode user-observable/accessibility-oriented testing practice.
rows.note: Full fragment exposed a distinct timing/absence semantic not explicit in the heading audit: getBy throws for missing synchronous content, findBy awaits asynchronous appearance, queryBy supports expected absence. Promoted to an explicit ready concept.

rows.title: Managing data on the server with the TanStack Query library
rows.selection_reason: Remote-cache ownership, query lifecycle and refetch behavior are core frontend server-state semantics.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: QueryClient/provider, queryKey identity, queryFn, pending/success data lifecycle and server-state ownership are covered by TanStack Query and server-vs-client-state concepts.

rows.title: Synchronizing data to the server using TanStack Query
rows.selection_reason: Mutation reconciliation/invalidation is a concurrency and cache-consistency boundary.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: mutationFn/mutate, stale cached result after server success and onSuccess invalidation/refetch are covered by mutation invalidation and remote mutation reconciliation concepts.

rows.title: useMemo
rows.selection_reason: Memoization is frequently cargo-culted; prose contains dependency/identity/performance caveats beyond the heading.
rows.note: Full fragment reviewed: rerender recomputation, dependency equality, memoized object/array identity and measure-before-memoize guidance are covered by useMemo plus render-cycle concepts and the ready card explicitly treats memoization as optimization rather than correctness.

rows.title: React/node-application security
rows.selection_reason: Security prose combines injection, XSS, dependency supply chain, access control and defense-in-depth guidance.
rows.note: Full security fragment reviewed. Existing concepts cover parameterized injection defense, React/untrusted rendering, vulnerable/supply-chain dependencies and server-side authorization. The final Helmet/defense-in-depth paragraph exposed a missing browser security-header concept, now mapped directly to BodySense Caddy/Nginx CSP/HSTS/nosniff/frame/referrer policy.
